categories.name: Moon notes
categories.description: The month, the sky and the window.

posts.title: A ring, from wire to wrist
posts.excerpt: A plain band takes about two hours of work and a week of waiting. Here is what happens at the bench.
posts.content:
A plain band takes about two hours of work and a week of waiting. Here is what happens at the bench.

Drawing and bending

We start with a length of recycled sterling wire, drawn down until it is just the right width, then bent around the mandrel to the size on the order.

The join is soldered once, with as little solder as it will take, so the seam disappears after filing.

Finishing

Filing, sanding with three papers, then a soft cloth: the ring is ready when it shines without glaring.

A good band should feel like it was always there.

Mio Kanzaki

posts.title: Polishing without a machine
posts.excerpt: Why every piece leaves the atelier polished by hand, and why we send a cloth with it.
posts.content:
Why every piece leaves the atelier polished by hand, and why we send a cloth with it.

A softer shine

Machine wheels leave a hard, mirror shine that shows every scratch. A cloth leaves a softer light that wears well.

It takes longer, and it is the part of the day we like best.

At home

The pale rose cloth in every box carries the same polish we use. A few strokes once a month are enough.

Silver should glow, not glitter.

Ren Oda

posts.title: The moonstone drawer
posts.excerpt: We keep our moonstones in one shallow drawer and choose each one by the window, in the late afternoon.
posts.content:
We keep our moonstones in one shallow drawer and choose each one by the window, in the late afternoon.

Choosing a stone

A good moonstone shows a soft blue light that seems to move under the surface. Many show none at all.

We look at each one in the same window light, and keep perhaps one in five.

Setting it

The stone sits in a small sterling cup with four claws, pressed over by hand so they hold without hiding it.

The stone decides; we only listen.

Mio Kanzaki

posts.title: Stacking three phases
posts.excerpt: Our Three Phase Stack began as three test rings left on one finger by accident.
posts.content:
Our Three Phase Stack began as three test rings left on one finger by accident.

Bright, brushed, hammered

Each band is finished differently, so the stack catches light like three nights of the same moon.

Worn together they read as one wide ring; apart, as three quiet ones.

Wearing them

Most people split the stack within a month: one on each hand, one passed on to someone else.

Three rings, one moon.

Ren Oda

posts.title: A chain cut to length
posts.excerpt: Every Pale Chain is cut from a longer coil on the day it is ordered, then closed with a small spring ring.
posts.content:
Every Pale Chain is cut from a longer coil on the day it is ordered, then closed with a small spring ring.

Why cut to order

A chain that is a little too long tangles; a little too short feels tight. We ask for your length and cut it there.

The ends are soldered so they never open.

Three lengths

Forty centimetres sits at the collarbone, forty-five just below, fifty for a pendant that should rest lower.

Length is a feeling before it is a number.

Mio Kanzaki

posts.title: The new moon window
posts.excerpt: Once a month, on the night of the new moon, we clear the bench and change the tray in the window.
posts.content:
Once a month, on the night of the new moon, we clear the bench and change the tray in the window.

A monthly habit

With no moon in the sky the street is darker, and the window glows more. It felt right to begin each month there.

New pieces go on the pale stone; the old ones go back in their pouches.

The letter

The same evening we write the short letter that goes out four times a year, with a small drawing of the coming moon.

A dark night is a good night to begin.

Ren Oda

Cut from sterling wire, soldered once, rounded and polished by hand. Made in your size within ten working days.

products.description:

Cast from recycled sterling in the atelier, then filed, satin-finished on the face and polished on the shoulders. Engraving of initials or a moon phase is free.

One round moonstone in a four-claw setting, on a fine 45 cm chain.

The stone is a pale rainbow moonstone, chosen one at a time for its blue light, and set in a hand-made sterling cup with four claws. The chain closes with a small ring clasp.

products.name: Pale Chain

products.description:
A fine cable chain on its own, or for any pendant you already love.

Small, even links that lie flat and catch the light softly. Choose 40, 45 or 50 cm when you order; the clasp is a sterling spring ring.

products.name: Tide Cuff
products.short: An open cuff of double half-round wire that follows the wrist like a tide line.
products.description:
An open cuff of double half-round wire that follows the wrist like a tide line.

Two lengths of sterling wire are soldered side by side, shaped on the bracelet mandrel and left open at the back, so it slips on sideways and can be eased to fit.

products.name: Waning Dome Ring
products.short: A heavier 5 mm domed band, darkened in the low places so it looks worn from the first day.
products.description:
A heavier 5 mm domed band, darkened in the low places so it looks worn from the first day.

Cast in sterling, domed on the outside, then oxidised and rubbed back by hand so only the high places shine, like the edge of a waning moon.

details.Size: Ring sizes 4 to 12 (US), made to order
details.Care: Do not polish the dark areas
